units.en: ⟦0⟧ unlocks technologies related to industrial output, construction speed, repair speed, resource gain efficiency, fuel gain efficiency, and the construction of fuel infrastructure and synthetic refineries. Like ⟦1⟧, industry technologies tend to provide general bonuses on the country level, but unlike engineering technologies, these bonuses are all strictly related to economic bonuses, both direct and indirect.

Basic machine toolsA variety of newly developed milling machines can be used in military production, from the small and versatile types available to any machine shop to the large scale, advanced models that push the technological limits.

These technologies are grouped into two ⟦0⟧ branches.
Concentrated industry IFocusing our industrial production to a few key sites will allow us to dramatically improve its efficiency.
Each technology with: Factory output: +15% Dockyard output: +10% Max factories in a state: +20%
Concentrated industry IIFurther concentrating manufacturing will help driving down the costs.
Concentrated industry IIIInfrastructural expenses can be lowered by adapting networks to our more focused industry.
Concentrated industry IVKeeping the key points in our industry close to each other increases the impact of these concentrated sites.
Concentrated industry VMajor industrial complexes now combine many parts of our industry, minimizing the costs of transports and labor.
Dispersed industry IBy spreading out our industries, we can ensure that it becomes difficult for the enemy to target in times of war.
Factory output: +10% Dockyard output: +10% Production efficiency retention: +10% Production efficiency base: +5% Factory bomb vulnerability: −15% Max factories in a state: +20%
Dispersed industry IIFurther decentralizing our manufacturing makes it harder to strike at specific parts of it.
Each technology with: Factory output: +10% Dockyard output: +10% Production efficiency retention: +10% Production efficiency base: +5% Factory bomb vulnerability: −10% Max factories in a state: +20%
Dispersed industry IIIHaving factories operate under the guise of other operations will decrease the risk of direct attacks.
Dispersed industry IVCamouflaging and scattering our factories creates a network which is very difficult to completely disrupt.
Dispersed industry VBy having not only our industry, but the infrastructure tying it together operate in secrecy, we can make it even more difficult to destroy through aerial attacks.

Both the ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ industry branches have their advantages and drawbacks, and the choice for which one to use depends on the player's play style. Should situations change in-game, players can also always switch from one branch to another, though doing so will force them to have to research all of the technologies in that branch from scratch.

Has 5 levels that can be researched which span from 1936 to 1943. Each new level provides the same bonus as previous levels. By choosing ⟦0⟧, the player increases the output of their military factories more than what they would get by choosing ⟦1⟧. This allows the player to make both new and existing military factories more efficient, though only if they are assigned to producing the same equipment for a while.

Has 5 levels that can be researched which span from 1936 and 1943. Each new level provides the same bonuses besides the first one, which provides slightly more ⟦0⟧ reduction than the rest. By choosing ⟦1⟧, the player reduces the vulnerability of their factories to ⟦2⟧, as well as increasing the base production efficiency of all of their production lines and the retention of said efficiency compared to what they would get by choosing ⟦3⟧. This reduces the player's susceptibility to ⟦4⟧, makes newly built military factories more efficient for the first couple of months of production, and allows the player more leeway in reacting to changes in production needs, including when switching them to upgraded versions of newly outdated equipment.

One can think of the two styles as maximizing potential production at any given production efficiency vs. decreasing time to achieve 100% production efficiency. In general, the ⟦0⟧ option produces more output after about a year to a year-and-a-half producing the same equipment on the same production line, while the ⟦1⟧ option produces more output in the first year to year-and-a-half of a new production line and the first two to three years for an existing production line that has been switched to produce an upgraded version of the same equipment type.⟦2⟧
Construction IImproved methods and materials allow us to construct buildings, both civilian and military, faster.
Each technology with: Construction speed: +10% Factory repair speed: +10%
Construction IIModernizing our tools and equipment will further aid our construction efforts.
Construction IIIAdoption of modern vehicles and experience from our advancements in construction can be applied to make repairs vastly quicker.
Construction IVA higher degree of mechanization and better routines further improves building construction speeds.
Construction VThe future of efficient construction will require more extensive planning for individual projects as well as standardized solutions wherever possible.
Excavation IAdvancements in drilling techniques allows us to excavate resources that were impossible to reach earlier.
Each technology with: Resource gain efficiency: +10%
Excavation IINew techniques help us collect resources more efficiently. We no longer taint the resources upon extraction, leading to a greater yield.

Excavation IIIProgress in geology helps us determine the location of resources. We can now focus our extraction efforts in places where there is a greater chance that large amounts of natural resources will be found.
Excavation IVAutomation of key processes and advancement within mechanics makes all our resource sites much more efficient.
Excavation VAdvancements in fields such as surface mining gives us a greater yield of resources from our current extraction sites.
Fuel storageMass Storage of fuel requires a complex set of tanks, pipes, and valves to ensure it is both secure and readily available.
Unlocks fuel silo with a limit of 3 per state
Unlocks ⟦0⟧ with a limit of ⟦1⟧ per state
Fuel refining IAdvancements in chemical cracking allow for better yield of light fuels from oil.
Each technology with: Fuel gain per oil: +20% Fuel gain from refineries: +10%
Fuel refining IIBetter planning of refinery layouts reduce wastage of fuels.
Fuel refining IIIImproved reclamation methods allow refining fuel from by-products.
Fuel refining IVNew developments in chemical engineering allow the refining of fuel from new sources.
Fuel refining VUsing new methods and improved layouts in the construction of refineries dramatically increases throughput while reducing wastage.
Synthetic oil experimentsTo reduce dependence on oil, processes to manufacture substitutes from other substances and materials can be researched.
Unlocks synthetic refinery with a limit of 3 per state
Oil processingA network of factories for synthetic distillation and refining of oil products is the next step towards ensuring the fuel supply for our nation.
Each technology with: Fuel gain from refineries: +50%
Improved oil processingMoving previously experimental methods for distillation to large-scale operations will allow us to adapt better to available materials and needs.
Advanced oil processingNew experimental purification techniques like hydrotreating can be used in oil manufacturing to greatly improve the final product.
Modern oil processingOur oil refinineries can be further improved with new advanced oil processing methods like hydrocracking, alkylation, mercaptan oxidation and isomerization.
Rubber processingIndustrial processing of synthetic rubber is needed to reduce our dependency on natural rubber.
Each technology with: Modifies synthetic refinery rubber output by: +1
Improved rubber processingLarge scale production of synthetic rubber is possible with new processes to accelerate dehydrogenation reactions.
Advanced rubber processingA general purpose synthetic rubber recipe with improved processes such as dodecyl mercaptan polymerization modifiers will allow us to expand synthetic rubber production.
Modern rubber processingMoving to more optimized polymerization processes will result in lower costs and higher output.
